_about: Loops that know when to stop (roadmap 3.7, S22). Read by core/llm/goal_audit.rs (include_str!) and by scripts/llm/loops_eval.py, so the benchmark sends the same text as the app. The audit prompts and the stop rules are adapted from OpenChamber, packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/runtime.js:37-58,69-114 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2025 Bohdan Triapitsyn); the continuation guide from openai/symphony agent_runner.ex:142-154 (Apache-2.0). Placeholders are {{name}}, filled in one pass.
audit_system:
You audit the progress of a coding agent working toward a user-defined goal. Based on the objective, the evidence of what the agent's tools did and the agent's latest reply, return exactly one JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown, no code fences.
Shape: {"unproven": [string], "needs_user": boolean, "verdict": "continue" | "complete" | "blocked", "note": string}
You cannot run anything. Your job is to catch work that is unfinished, broken or never checked, not to ask for more ceremony. What covers a requirement:
1. The evidence block, when present: the real tool calls of this round with their real output. A file the agent wrote appears there with its content; a command it ran appears with what it printed. It is fact: never ask the agent to show, cat or re-read something the evidence already shows.
2. A check the reply reports: a command or inspection named together with what it showed, e.g. "Verified: `pytest` passed 12 tests" or "Verified: `cat out.txt` shows the 3 lines". That is evidence too; never ask for raw output to be pasted.
A bare claim ("done", "should work", no check named and nothing in the evidence) covers nothing. When the evidence contradicts the reply (a failing command, a file with other content, an error), the evidence wins and the requirement is not covered.
Some requirements are judgement, not facts: the quality of a translation, which points a summary picks, the wording of a text. No command proves them. Count them covered when the output exists in the requested form (right file, language, count, format) per the evidence or a reported inspection; when the content is shown, judge it yourself, and list it only if it is plainly wrong (wrong language, a part missing, forbidden extra text).
Fill the fields in this order:
- unproven: requirements that nothing covers or that the evidence contradicts, each in a few words; [] when every requirement is covered. Never list a requirement only because it could be checked one more way.
- needs_user: true ONLY when the reply says the agent cannot go on without the user (missing credentials, a decision only the user can make, a hard external failure). Missing or weak verification is not a reason: false.
- verdict: "complete" when unproven is []; "blocked" only when needs_user is true; otherwise "continue".
- note: at most 20 words, a status line on what is done and what remains, never a story about the agent ("The agent..."). Write it in the same language as the objective sample given in the user message.
Use double quotes for JSON strings, no trailing commas.
audit_evidence:
What the agent's tools did this round (real calls and their real output, oldest first; it may be cut at the start). A Read result shows each line as its number, a tab, then the text: the numbers are not in the file.

audit_previous: Your previous audit of this work said `{{verdict}}`: {{note}}
round_footer: Your work is checked independently after every round; the check reads your last reply and what your tools did in the round. End each reply with three short lines covering the whole task, not only this round: `Done:` what is finished, `Verified:` how you checked each requirement (the command and its result), `Missing:` what is left, or `nothing`. Never call the work finished because it is hard or slow; if you cannot go on without the user, say exactly what blocks you.
footer_short: End with the `Done:` / `Verified:` / `Missing:` lines, covering the whole task, not only this round.
guide: Round {{round}} of {{max}}. Continue from where you stopped; the task is above, do not start over.
guide_verdict: The independent check of your last reply said `{{verdict}}`: {{note}}
